business_problem: Target needs to keep products available across stores and digital channels while making shopping more personalized and efficient for guests, especially during high-demand periods such as the holiday season.
solution_summary: Target describes an in-house machine-learning stack embedded in its core retail operations rather than a standalone AI product. Upstream signals include store transactions, online orders, Drive Up interactions, guest service center activity, and demand patterns across physical and digital channels. Target says AI inside its supply chain and inventory management systems forecasts product demand, detects "unknown" out-of-stock situations, and helps place inventory in the right locations as demand changes. On the customer side, those operational insights support personalized experiences delivered through Target Circle, Target.com, the Target app, and Roundel, where guests are shown relevant products, deals, and product ads. The article does not identify a storage platform or model-serving framework, but it makes clear that AI is integrated into the systems that power store, web, app, and merchandising experiences.
products_used: supply chain and inventory management systems

solution_components.name: supply chain and inventory management systems
solution_components.role: These systems use AI to forecast demand, detect unknown out-of-stock conditions, and position inventory where it is needed as demand shifts.

solution_components.name: Target Circle
solution_components.role: Target's loyalty program is one of the channels where AI personalizes the products and deals shown to guests.

solution_components.name: Target.com
solution_components.role: The ecommerce site uses AI to help guests find the products and deals most relevant to them.

solution_components.name: Roundel
solution_components.role: Target's retail media business uses AI to connect guests with brands through product ad placements.

solution_components.name: Target app
solution_components.role: The app presents AI-selected offers and product suggestions tailored to the individual guest.

data_flow: Store transactions, online orders, Drive Up interactions, guest service center activity, and demand signals feed AI embedded in Target's supply chain and inventory management systems. Those models forecast demand, flag unknown out-of-stocks, and guide inventory placement. Outputs are then surfaced to guests through Target Circle, Target.com, the Target app, and Roundel product ad placements.
business_outcome: Target says AI helps keep holiday gifts and essentials in stock, improves the relevance of products and deals shown to guests, supports faster and more efficient operations, and gives store teams more time to serve guests.
architecture_clues: Target says it has used AI for many years across supply chain, inventory management, checkout, website, and app experiences.
The company describes a long-built internal infrastructure that lets teams move quickly and experiment continuously with AI.
The article mentions team-facing and guest-facing AI use cases, while generative AI remains in exploration rather than described production use.
evidence_quotes: "We've been using AI for many years to support our team and drive speed and efficiency across all our operations - everything from our supply chain and inventory management systems all the way to applications in the checkout lines in our stores and on our website and app."
"AI helps us ensure our guests find the holiday gifts and essentials they need by forecasting product demand and keeping items from going out of stock."
"It even helps us predict and correct when a store has an unknown out-of-stock item"
"We do it via Target Circle - our loyalty program - and on Target.com, helping guests find the products and deals that are most relevant to them."
"That includes connecting our guests to the brands they love through product ad placements through our retail media business, Roundel."
